evidence.answer: Based on the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation Act, the appointment of any board member, including a president's daughter, must comply with specific legal provisions. The Act requires that non-ex-officio members appointed by the National Council of Ministers must be "persons who by reason of their ability, experience or specialised knowledge of the oil industry or of business or professional attainments are capable of making useful contributions to the work of the Corporation." Furthermore, board members have a duty to disclose any conflicts of interest and must "take no part in any deliberation or decision of the Board relating to such contract or arrangement" where they have an interest. Therefore, compliance depends on whether the appointee meets the qualification criteria and whether proper conflict-of-interest procedures are followed; the Act does not explicitly prohibit such an appointment but mandates these governance standards.
